title: Oct 10 Results + Oct 11 Preview: Perfect Start to October Baseball
summary: Cleveland delivers as expected. Now we turn to Milwaukee's home stand.

content.value:
## October 10 Recap: When Experience Meets Execution

You know, I've been doing this long enough to appreciate a clean slate when I see one. Yesterday we went 1-0, and while the sample size was small, the execution was textbook. The Guardians took care of business at home against the Sox, just like we projected at 53% confidence. Nothing fancy, nothing lucky—just good baseball played the way it's supposed to be in October.

## The Cleveland Story

There's something about Cleveland in October that reminds me of teams from a different era. They don't beat you with flash—they grind you down with fundamentals and home-field execution. The 53% confidence wasn't a slam dunk, but it reflected what the data was telling us: a slight edge for the home team that knew how to leverage it.

I've seen plenty of postseason series where the visiting team comes in hot and steals Game 1. This wasn't one of those nights. The Guardians controlled the tempo from the first pitch, and our model caught that edge before the game even started.

## Looking Ahead: October 11 Top Pick

Now we shift our focus to Milwaukee, where things get interesting. The Dodgers roll into town, and on paper, you'd think Los Angeles has every advantage. But here's what I've learned over the years: October baseball at Miller Park—excuse me, American Family Field—is a different beast entirely.

Our model is leaning Brewers at 61% confidence, and I'll tell you why that number makes sense.

content.title: ⭐ Tomorrow's Top Pick - October 11
content.sub: vs Los Angeles Dodgers • Home advantage meets pitching depth

content.value:
## The Pitching Matchup: Skubal vs Misiorowski

Tarik Skubal for the Dodgers—now there's a name that commands respect. The guy has been dealing all season, and Los Angeles didn't acquire him to lose playoff games. But Jacob Misiorowski on the Milwaukee side? If you've been paying attention to what the Brewers have been developing, you know this kid has the stuff to hang with anyone.

I've seen this script before: veteran arm for the visiting team, rising talent at home with something to prove. The edge goes to Milwaukee not because Skubal isn't excellent—he is—but because Misiorowski has been lights-out in this park, and the Brewers' offense has shown they can manufacture runs in tight games.

## Why 61% Feels Right

Six out of ten times, Milwaukee wins this game. That's what the model says, and from where I sit, it tracks. The Brewers have home-field advantage, a starter who's been terrific in high-leverage situations, and a bullpen that's fresher than people think.

This isn't a coinflip, but it's not a lock either. The Dodgers are too talented to dismiss. But if I'm putting my reputation on the line—and after 20-plus years of covering this game, I am—I'm riding with Milwaukee tomorrow.

Let's see if we can make it 2-0 to start this October run.
